From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Subject: Quarterline steer and dependency swap request

Team —

Quick leadership / OKR check-in ahead of the QBR prep window. I pulled a short status + asks and highlighted a dependency swap that I think preserves delivery while lowering risk for the quarterline. Please scan and reply with commitments by EOD Wed so I can lock the QBR narrative.

High-level OKR health (top-level):
- Product: Model-serving throughput (OKR KPT) — amber. Current throughput improvements + batching gains expected to hit 65% of the target by EOW; two infra blockers remain (see dependency list).
- Reliability: 99.9% availability target — red on current trajectory due to region failover test backlog and a known GPU driver regression impacting one Dedicated pool.
- Go-to-market: Two pilot expansions (Astra Metrics, Luma Health) are on-track; Astra requires a minor SLA addendum before committing to Dedicated in Q1.

Proposed re-scope (to keep the QBR story crisp):
1) Push non-critical 99th-pct latency optimization (workstream: attention-kern) from this quarter to Q1; retain 95th improvement effort this quarter.
2) Move experimental quantization profile rollout for large-llama from broad canary to targeted customers only.
3) Prioritize region failover + Dedicated pool driverfix as top infra asks (these are blocking reliability OKR).

Dependency swap request (concrete):
- Ask: Naomi/Markus — can we reassign 0.6 FTE of the attention-kern resource (Ben_Carter's allocation) for the next 6 weeks to the driver/regression work? In exchange, we will bump the attention-kern timeline to Q1 and commit Product to a smaller public benchmark update in December.
- Rationale: The driver/regression currently threatens the Dedicated SLA and the Astra pilot. Losing Astra would materially change our QBR net-new ARR narrative.

Attachments: QBR_prep_deck_v3.pptx (draft narrative), Dependency_Matrix_v2.xlsx (current owner matrix + riskiest items).

Decisions I need by EOD Wed:
- Yes/no on the 0.6 FTE swap and who covers attention-kern while reallocated.
- Any objections to explicitly calling out Astra's SLA addendum as a QBR risk.

Thanks — I tried to keep this tight. If helpful, I can run a 15-min triage right after stand.

-Vanessa
VP, Product & Operations
Redwood Inference
